Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.

The nature of a typical car assembly plant has changed. The industry has fewer firms, operates on larger sites and has more automated machinery. How is this change most likely to have affected the relative use of factors of production in the industry? increased relative use decreased relative use

options.A: capital and enterprise labour and land
options.B: enterprise and labour land and capital
options.C: labour and land capital and enterprise
options.D: land and capital enterprise and labour

questions.questionText: Which item would be least likely to be classed as land?

options.A: fertilisers
options.B: fisheries
options.C: forests
options.D: coal

questions.questionText: Why does the concept of scarcity apply to the use of fossil fuels?

options.A: Demand fluctuates according to price changes.
options.B: Supply is insufficient to meet demand.
options.C: Their use is restricted because of harmful pollution.
options.D: They are being replaced by renewable energy sources.

questions.questionText: An economist knows the current point at which an economy operates within its production possibility curve. What can the economist conclude about this economy?

options.A: its degree of self-sufficiency
options.B: its international competitiveness
options.C: its level of output of two goods
options.D: its rate of economic growth

questions.questionText: An increase in which factor is likely to cause a shift to the left of the demand curve for cinema movies?

options.A: expenses for the heating system in the cinema
options.B: payments charged by movie scriptwriters
options.C: the cost of transport to the cinema
options.D: taxes on the incomes of cinema operators

questions.questionText: Four firms supply the market. The market supply is 50 units at $20 and 100 units at $40. The table shows the market share of each firm at the two prices. Which firm does not have a normal upward-sloping supply curve? % market share % market share at $20 at $40

options.A: Demand for an inferior good has a positive relationship to income and a negative relationship to price.

options.C: Demand for a normal good has a positive relationship to income and a positive relationship to price.
options.D: Demand for a normal good has a negative relationship to income and a positive relationship to price.

questions.questionText: A firm calculates that the income elasticity of demand for its product is –3.0. What can be deduced from this information?

options.A: In a period of economic growth, its total revenue should increase.
options.B: In a period of economic recession, its total revenue should increase.
options.C: It has few substitutes so it should increase its price to increase total revenue.
options.D: It has many substitutes so it should decrease price to increase total revenue.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand and supply curves for the global air cargo market. The initial equilibrium is at point X. What would the new equilibrium be if there is a global recession and an increase in fuel costs? price S S

options.A: S
options.D: D 1 3 O quantity

questions.questionText: A government gives free food to poor households in a community. What is this food an example of?

options.A: a free good
options.B: a public good
options.C: a demerit good
options.D: a normal good

questions.questionText: A government wishes to raise the incomes of farmers without raising the price of food to consumers. Which policy should it use?

options.A: a maximum price below the market price for food
options.B: a minimum price below the market price for food
options.C: a payment of a subsidy to farmers to produce food
options.D: a release of government food stocks onto the market

questions.questionText: Governments in market economies give different reasons for intervening in the operation of an economy. Which reason given is a normative statement?

options.A: Average incomes have failed to keep pace with price rises during the past year.
options.B: Energy prices have increased by more than 50% during the past year.
options.C: The distribution of incomes has become more unfair during the past year.
options.D: The poorest 10% of households have suffered the greatest fall in average real income during the past year.

questions.questionText: The table illustrates macroeconomic data for an economy. All figures are in $ billions. What is the equilibrium real output? consumption government investment exports imports real output expenditure expenditure
A country’s net national income (NNI) is less than its gross national income (GNI). What does this mean?

options.A: incomes earned overseas were less than incomes sent overseas
options.B: inflation has been accounted for in NNI but not in GNI
options.C: the country’s exports decreased
options.D: there has been a net depreciation in the value of the country’s fixed capital assets

questions.questionText: Asha is currently unemployed. She has been offered a job but has decided to decline the offer and search for a better paid job. Which type of unemployment is this?

options.A: cyclical
options.B: frictional
options.C: seasonal
options.D: structural

questions.questionText: A major trading nation, country X, is in equilibrium at the full employment level of real output. There is then a recession in its main international markets. What are the most likely consequences of this change for country X? rate of inflation unemployment

options.A: decrease decrease
options.B: decrease increase
options.C: unchanged decrease
options.D: unchanged increase

questions.questionText: Why would a fall in a country's average price level cause its aggregate demand curve to slope downwards?

options.A: It leads to an increase in interest rates.
options.B: It reduces the real value of money balances.
options.C: It makes the country’s goods cheaper relative to foreign goods.
options.D: It leads to the expectation of further price falls.

questions.questionText: To counter deflation a central bank uses expansionary monetary policy. What is likely to result?

options.A: a higher cost of borrowing
options.B: an increase in aggregate demand
options.C: an appreciation of the exchange rate
options.D: an increase in government debt

questions.questionText: Which statement about government budget surpluses and deficits is the most accurate?

options.A: A surplus implies that the balance of payments is in surplus.
options.B: A surplus implies that the government is spending too much money.
options.C: A deficit implies that the economy is in decline.
options.D: A deficit implies that the national debt is increasing.

questions.questionText: What is most likely to decrease if a government uses expansionary fiscal policy?

options.A: a balance of payments deficit
options.B: cyclical unemployment
options.C: the level of wages
options.D: the rate of inflation

questions.questionText: Sweden had a change in its Consumer Prices Index (CPI) of –0.6%. Which combination of policies might its government use to restore price stability?

options.A: increase interest rates and increase indirect taxes
options.B: increase interest rates and reduce government spending
options.C: reduce government spending and increase income tax
options.D: reduce interest rates and increase government spending

questions.questionText: What is a disadvantage of operating a floating exchange rate system?

options.A: It makes it difficult to prioritise domestic economic policy aims.
options.B: It makes the prices of internationally traded goods less predictable.
options.C: It means that the government must keep significant foreign currency reserves.
options.D: It requires continuous government intervention in currency markets.

questions.questionText: What is not an example of protectionism?

options.A: export subsidies
options.B: import subsidies
options.C: quotas
options.D: tariffs

options.A: They are an effective way of raising revenue.
options.B: They improve the balance of payments on a current account.
options.C: They improve a nation’s terms of trade in a bilateral agreement.
